metadata.title: Knife Steel Database
metadata.composition_units: weight percent (wt%), nominal/typical values from manufacturer datasheets. Where a datasheet gives a range, the midpoint is listed. Elements not listed are unspecified or trace. Values with composition_confidence = 'approximate' are proprietary alloys where the maker has not published a full spec.
metadata.ratings_scale: 1 (worst) to 10 (best), relative to the whole knife-steel population. edge_retention ~ CATRA / wear-resistance class at typical hardness; toughness ~ unnotched Charpy class at typical hardness; corrosion_resistance ~ pitting/salt-water class; ease_of_sharpening ~ inverse of carbide volume/hardness.
metadata.hrc: Typical as-used blade hardness range (Rockwell C) in production and custom knives. Many steels can be run outside this band.
sources: Crucible Industries datasheets (CPM S30V, S35VN, S45VN, S90V, S110V, S125V, MagnaCut, 3V, 4V, 10V, 15V, M4, CruWear, REX 45, REX 121, 154CM, CPM 154, 20CV, SPY27)
voestalpine Bohler Edelstahl datasheets (M390, M398, N690, N680, N695, K110, K390, K720, Elmax, Vanax SuperClean)
Uddeholm datasheets (AEB-L, Sleipner, Vanadis 4 Extra, Vanadis 8, 26C3)
Carpenter Technology datasheets (CTS-BD1, CTS-BD1N, CTS-XHP, CTS-204P, CTS-40CP, Maxamet)
Hitachi Metals / Proterial YSS datasheets (ATS-34, ATS-55, ZDP-189, HAP40, HAP72, YXR7, Ginsan, Shirogami, Aogami, SLD, SK-5)
Takefu Special Steel (VG-1, VG-10, VG-MAX, SG2/R2)
Zapp (LC200N/Cronidur 30, Z-Wear), Lohmann (Niolox), Buderus/NJSB (Nitro-V), Erasteel, Aubert & Duval (X15TN), Daido (Cowry-X), Damasteel (RWL34, DS93X)
ASTM/AISI/SAE, DIN EN ISO 4957, JIS G4401/G4403, GB/T 1220 standard compositions for generic grades
Knife Steel Nerds (knifesteelnerds.com) steel ratings & composition articles; zknives.com knife steel chart; BladeHQ / Knife Center steel guides for brand usage

steels.name: 420HC
steels.notes: Buck's Paul Bos heat treat gets the most out of it. Fine-grained, very easy to sharpen.

steels.name: 420J2
steels.notes: Very soft; mostly used for cladding, cheap knives and dive knives.

steels.name: 440A
steels.notes: Mn and Si listed are maximums.

steels.name: 440C
steels.notes: Large primary chromium carbides limit toughness. Mn, Si, Ni listed as maximums.

steels.name: 425M
steels.notes: Largely replaced by 420HC.

steels.name: 12C27
steels.notes: Very fine carbide structure; excellent edge stability for its class.

steels.name: 13C26
steels.notes: Essentially AEB-L; razor-blade steel.

steels.name: 14C28N
steels.notes: Nitrogen-enhanced 13C26 developed with Kershaw; current budget benchmark.

steels.name: AEB-L
steels.notes: Finest carbide structure of any common stainless; toughest stainless. Favorite of custom kitchen makers.

steels.name: Nitro-V
steels.manufacturer: Buderus Edelstahl (for New Jersey Steel Baron)
steels.notes: AEB-L with N and V additions for hardenability and grain refinement.

steels.name: AUS-10
steels.notes: Comparable to 440C / VG-10 class.

steels.name: 8Cr13MoV
steels.notes: Chinese near-equivalent of AUS-8.

steels.name: 9Cr18MoV
steels.notes: Chinese 440C analogue.

steels.name: 7Cr17MoV
steels.notes: Chinese 440A analogue.

steels.name: 3Cr13
steels.notes: Chinese 420J2 analogue.

steels.name: 5Cr15MoV
steels.notes: Chinese analogue of German 1.4116.

steels.name: 10Cr15CoMoV
steels.notes: Chinese VG-10 clone, usually in 67-layer 'Damascus' kitchen knives.

steels.name: VG-10
steels.notes: Cobalt improves hardenability; prone to micro-chipping if ground too thin.

steels.name: VG-MAX
steels.notes: Proprietary VG-10 variant with slightly more Cr, V and W; exact spec unpublished.

steels.name: 154CM
steels.notes: Originally developed for jet-engine bearings; ATS-34 is the Hitachi equivalent.

steels.name: ATS-55
steels.notes: Low-Mo cost-reduced ATS-34; discontinued.

steels.name: CTS-BD1
steels.notes: Similar in class to 440B/AUS-8 but cleaner and finer-grained.

steels.name: CTS-BD1N
steels.notes: Nitrogen-alloyed BD1; reaches 1-2 HRC higher than BD1.

steels.name: N690
steels.notes: European VG-10/440C class steel; staple of Italian knives.

steels.name: N680
steels.notes: Nitrogen-alloyed, salt-water oriented.

steels.name: N695
steels.notes: Bohler's 440C.

steels.name: H1
steels.notes: Austenitic, essentially rust-proof; hardness from cold rolling, not heat treatment. Serrated edges work-harden to ~65 HRC locally.

steels.name: H2
steels.notes: Successor to H1; Spyderco states it is functionally equivalent to H1 with a revised mill process. Full spec unpublished; H1 values shown.

steels.name: LC200N
steels.notes: Nitrogen replaces most carbon; aerospace bearing steel. Essentially immune to salt-water corrosion.

steels.name: Niolox
steels.notes: Niobium carbides give fine structure with good toughness.
Standard German kitchen-knife steel.

steels.name: MBS-26
steels.notes: Proprietary; comparable to 440B/Ginsan.

steels.name: Ginsan
steels.notes: Stainless that sharpens like a carbon steel; favorite for Japanese single-bevel stainless knives.

steels.name: ZA-18
steels.notes: Aichi's answer to VG-10; richer in Cr, Mo and Co.

steels.name: 440XH
steels.notes: Ingot version of what CTS-XHP is in powder form.

steels.name: AR-RPM9
steels.notes: Proprietary PM stainless marketed as 'budget powder steel'; performs similar to VG-10/BD1N.

steels.name: CPM 154
steels.notes: Powder version of 154CM; much tougher and more uniform.

steels.name: RWL34
steels.notes: Named after Robert W. Loveless; essentially CPM 154 with a V addition.

steels.name: M390
steels.notes: 20CV and CTS-204P are compositionally identical.

steels.name: CPM 20CV
steels.notes: US-made M390 equivalent.

steels.name: CTS-204P
steels.notes: Carpenter's M390 equivalent.

steels.name: M398
steels.notes: Higher-wear successor to M390; competes with S110V/S125V class.

steels.name: CPM S30V
steels.notes: First steel designed specifically for knives (2001, Crucible + Chris Reeve).

steels.name: CPM S35VN
steels.notes: Niobium replaces some V for toughness and machinability.

steels.name: CPM S45VN
steels.notes: Higher Cr + N for better corrosion resistance than S35VN.

steels.name: CPM S60V
steels.notes: Discontinued; usually run soft (55-57) for toughness.

steels.name: CPM S125V
steels.notes: Very difficult to grind; limited production.

steels.name: CPM MagnaCut
steels.notes: Released 2021. Designed so all Cr stays in solution (no chromium carbides): corrosion resistance of S110V with toughness of 4V/CruWear.

steels.name: CPM SPY27
brands: Spyderco (Para 3, Manix 2, Native 5, Shaman, Lil' Native)
steels.notes: Spyderco proprietary, between S35VN and S30V in wear with better toughness.

steels.name: Vanax SuperClean
steels.notes: Nitrogen-based (vanadium nitrides); best corrosion resistance of any high-performance stainless. Third-generation Vanax, replaced Vanax 35 and Vanax 75.

steels.name: CTS-XHP
steels.notes: Described as 'stainless D2'; behaves like PM 440C at higher hardness.

steels.name: CTS-40CP
steels.notes: Powder-metallurgy 440C.

steels.name: ZDP-189
steels.notes: Most Cr tied up in carbides, so only moderately stainless despite 20% Cr. Usually laminated.

steels.name: Cowry-X
steels.notes: Near-identical to ZDP-189.

steels.name: SG2 / R2
steels.notes: The dominant PM stainless in Japanese kitchen knives.

steels.name: SRS-15
steels.notes: Semi-stainless PM; SRS-13 is the slightly lower-carbon sibling. Full spec not published by Nachi.

steels.name: D2
steels.notes: 'Semi-stainless' air-hardening die steel; large chromium carbides. Hugely popular in Chinese production knives.

steels.name: K110
steels.notes: Bohler's D2 (DIN 1.2379).

steels.name: A2
steels.notes: Air-hardening; good balance of toughness and edge holding for bushcraft/fixed blades.

steels.name: O1
steels.notes: Oil-hardening; the classic beginner knifemaker steel.

steels.name: K720
steels.notes: Bohler's AISI O2.

steels.name: W1
steels.notes: Water-hardening; C ranges 0.7-1.5 depending on grade. Cr, V, Ni listed are maximums.

steels.name: W2
steels.notes: W1 with vanadium for grain refinement; shallow hardening gives dramatic hamons.

steels.name: L6
steels.notes: Saw-blade steel; exceptionally tough, especially as bainite.

steels.name: 15N20
steels.notes: Bandsaw steel; the standard bright layer in 1084/15N20 pattern-welded Damascus.

steels.name: M2
steels.notes: Classic high-speed steel; usually black-coated for rust protection.

steels.name: CPM M4
steels.notes: Popular competition-cutting steel; excellent toughness for its wear resistance.

steels.name: CPM REX 45
steels.notes: Cobalt HSS, roughly a PM version of M42/HAP40.

steels.name: CPM REX 121
steels.notes: Highest wear resistance of any commercial knife steel; extremely brittle.

steels.name: Maxamet
steels.notes: Tungsten-based HSS; will rust readily. Diamond stones required.

steels.name: HAP40
steels.notes: Japanese equivalent of REX 45; usually stainless-clad in kitchen knives.

steels.name: YXR7
steels.notes: Low-carbide matrix HSS; very tough at high hardness.

steels.name: CPM 3V
steels.notes: The benchmark hard-use fixed-blade steel; toughness close to 5160 at 60 HRC.

steels.name: CPM 4V
steels.notes: Near-equivalent of Vanadis 4 Extra.

steels.name: Vanadis 8
steels.notes: Third-generation PM; competes with 10V/K390 with better toughness.

steels.name: CPM 10V
steels.notes: Original (1978) vanadium-carbide PM steel; K390 is Bohler's version.

steels.name: CPM 15V
steels.notes: Highest vanadium content of any commercial steel (~30% carbide volume).

steels.name: CPM CruWear
steels.notes: Descendant of Vasco Wear; Z-Wear (Zapp) is the same composition.

steels.name: Z-Wear
steels.notes: Zapp's equivalent of CPM CruWear.

steels.name: Sleipner
steels.notes: Tougher, finer-grained alternative to D2 with less Cr.

steels.name: INFI
steels.notes: Values are those published by Busse; independent analyses vary. Nitrogen-alloyed, low-carbon, very tough.
Workhorse US carbon steel; shallow-hardening, needs fast quench. P and S are maximums.

steels.name: 1095 Cro-Van
steels.notes: 1095 with Cr, V and Ni for hardenability and grain refinement.
Eutectoid; simplest steel to heat treat well. Dark layer in 1084/15N20 Damascus.
Machete and large-chopper steel.
Sword and kukri steel.
Leaf-spring steel; extremely tough. Spring-steel category.
Silicon spring steel; famous for flex recovery in swords.
Bearing steel; very fine carbide structure, excellent edge stability at high hardness.

steels.name: 80CrV2
steels.notes: Tough, easy-to-heat-treat 1084 alternative with Cr/V; common in European bushcraft knives.

steels.name: SK-5
brands: Cold Steel (SK-5 line: SRK, Recon Scout, Trail Master)
steels.notes: Japanese equivalent of 1080/1084.
Large bandsaw steel; among the toughest knife steels (similar to L6 / 15N20).

steels.name: 26C3
steels.notes: Razor-blade steel; Western equivalent of Shirogami #1.

steels.name: T10
steels.notes: Chinese W1-class tool steel widely used for clay-tempered swords.

steels.name: Aogami Super
steels.notes: Highest-performance Yasugi carbon steel; usually clad in soft iron or stainless.

steels.name: Aogami #2
steels.notes: Most widely used Aogami grade.

steels.name: Shirogami #1
steels.notes: Ultra-pure plain carbon; takes the keenest edge of any common steel. Demanding heat treat.

steels.name: Shirogami #2
steels.notes: Most common Japanese kitchen carbon steel.

steels.name: Kigami #2
steels.notes: Lower-purity Yasugi grade (more P/S than Shirogami).

steels.name: Damasteel DS93X
steels.notes: Composition shown is the 50/50 average; see composition_layers. Performs like RWL34/CPM 154. Many patterns (Rose, Ladder, Bifrost, Vinland).

steels.name: VG-10 Damascus
steels.manufacturer: Takefu Special Steel / various Seki and Tsubame-Sanjo mills

composition_layers.cladding: alternating SUS410/SUS405-class soft stainless with nickel layers (not hardened; cosmetic)

steels.notes: Cutting performance equals plain VG-10; the Damascus is cladding only.

steels.name: 1084/15N20 Damascus
steels.manufacturer: Various (Alabama Damascus, Vegas Forge, Baker Forge, custom smiths)
steels.notes: Other common carbon Damascus mixes: 1095/15N20, 5160/15N20/52100 (Alabama), O1/L6. Performance roughly that of the weaker layer.

steels.name: Zirconia Ceramic
steels.process: sintered (white) or hot isostatic pressed (black) yttria-stabilized zirconia
steels.hardness_note: ~1200-1300 HV (Vickers), ~8.5 Mohs; outside the Rockwell C scale, roughly 'HRC 80+' equivalent. Not a steel.
steels.notes: Non-ferrous; never rusts, holds an edge extremely long but chips/shatters on impact and cannot be sharpened on normal stones (diamond only).

steels.name: CPM S30V (Buck/Paul Bos HT)
steels.notes: Duplicate composition of id 55; kept as separate record only for brand-mapping purposes. Delete if not wanted.
